books.section: Topic 7.7 1920s: Innovations in Communication and Technology

primary_sources: Ford Model T advertisement, LIFE magazine, October 1908
Bruce Barton, The Man Nobody Knows (1925)

stimulus.text: The advertisement, from LIFE magazine, October 1908, shows an open five-passenger touring car at the top. Its headline reads: “The Ford Four Cylinder, Twenty Horse Power, Five Passenger Touring Car $850.00 Fob. Detroit.” Above the headline it says: “HIGH PRICED QUALITY IN A LOW PRICED CAR.” At the bottom: “Ford Motor Company, Detroit.”
stimulus.source_note: Ford Model T advertisement, LIFE magazine, October 1908, via The Henry Ford (Flickr), CC BY-SA 2.0. The headline and price are the advertiser's own wording.

options.text: failed to change how Americans thought at all
options.misconception: Barton shows advertising changing how Americans thought, even about religion. It did not fail; it spread everywhere.

been banned from all books and magazines
options.misconception: Advertising was never banned from books. Barton's book itself was a bestseller that used advertising ideas.

options.text: replaced religion in American life for good
options.misconception: Barton mixed religion and advertising; he did not replace religion. His book treated faith as a sales story.

rationales.A: Barton shows advertising changing how Americans thought, even about religion. It did not fail; it spread everywhere.
rationales.B: Background from the books: Barton's book called Jesus a “super-salesman” and treated Christianity as a marketing triumph. Advertising had moved from selling goods into American culture itself.
rationales.C: Advertising was never banned from books. Barton's book itself was a bestseller that used advertising ideas.
rationales.D: Barton mixed religion and advertising; he did not replace religion. His book treated faith as a sales story.
rationales.general:
1. Recall what Barton did: he wrote about Jesus as a salesman, not about a product.
2. Ask what that means: advertising ideas had left the marketplace and entered religion.
3. Name the change: the ad in the stimulus sold a car, while Barton sold a faith with the same tools.
Remember: when a method shows up far from where it started, it has become part of the culture.
